title: The constant regular uniformizer and its prescribed transported scalar
statement: For a prime l, finite extension E of Q_l and any scheme X, use the ring O, residue q and prescribed module transport F of [def-sfb-internal-completion-section-transport] and [def-sfb-internal-quotient-tower-model]. There exists one global section t of O such that kernelIdeal(q)(U)=span(t(U)) on every object U and multiplication by t(U) on O(U) is injective. For every endomorphism d of the point regular integer module acting on continuous sections as multiplication by the chosen uniformizer, every integral complex P and n>=0, with N=complex(P), U:Tot(N tensor O[0])=N the right unitor, one has F(scalar(d,n,P)) followed by U.inv = U.inv followed by ringedSingletonKoszulPower(O,t,N,n). The scalar and tensor expressions are those of [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus] and [lem-sfb-ringed-singleton-koszul-cone]. There is no arbitrary generating section or unspecified change of basis in this assertion.

source.place: Lemma derived-completion-koszul (0A0E), rank-one scalar comparison; literature/blueprint/latest/blueprint/sec-six-functors-basics/sk-thm-sf-pf-adic/sk-thm-sf-pf-adic-open.proof.md, reduction paragraph.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary single-uniformizer scalar comparison to obtain compatible integer and first-residue ring isomorphisms e and f, and the action equation on ordinary modules. Let t be the image under e of the constant chosen uniformizer.

On every object V, the quotient square identifies the residue kernel with the image under the ring isomorphism e(V) of the constant quotient kernel. The proved finite_kernel formula identifies that kernel with the span of the constant uniformizer; Ideal.map_span and Set.image_singleton give exactly span(t(V)). This is the private uniformizerSection_kernel proof.

The DVR theorem identifies the span of the chosen uniformizer with the nonzero maximal ideal, hence the uniformizer is nonzero. Multiplication by it is injective on the lifted coefficient DVR. Apply the proved constantScalar_ring_injective lemma, then transport sectionwise injectivity along e(V), using that e(V) preserves multiplication. This is the private uniformizerSection_regular proof; it requires no nontriviality of the section rings.

The scalarOnModules expression is conjugation of the pulled-back regular-module endomorphism followed by tensoringLeft. Functoriality and cancellation of the two isomorphisms prove that it preserves natural-number powers. Evaluation on a module and the prescribed transport preserve these powers too. Induct on k to deduce a^k followed by v equals v followed by b^k from the one-scalar intertwining equation. Apply this with k=n+1 and the right unitor; tensoring by the rank-one scalar preserves powers.

Check the resulting complex equation degreewise. Mathlib rightUnitor'_inv writes the inverse unitor in degree q as the ordinary inverse unitor, tensoring with singleObjXSelf.inv, and the (q,0) coproduct inclusion. The ι_mapBifunctorMap and single_map_f_self formulas move the single scalar across that inclusion. The ordinary powered equation and cancellation of singleObjXSelf.inv followed by its hom prove the equality. This requires neither boundedness nor flatness and proves the actual prescribed total-tensor equality.

theorem uniformizer_scalar_realization :
    ∃ t : ((ring l E X).obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections,
      (∀ U : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, u} X,
        (ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (residue l E X)).sections U =
          Ideal.span {t.val (op U)}) ∧
      (∀ U : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, u} X,
        Function.Injective (fun x : (ring l E X).obj.obj (op U) ↦ t.val (op U) * x)) ∧
      ∀ (d : End (Mod.regular (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E))),
        (∀ (S : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ) (b : (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E).obj.obj S)
          (s : S.unop), ((d.hom.hom.app S) b).down s =
            Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E * b.down s) →
        ∀ (P : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ) (n : ℕ),
          ((modules l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
              (PrincipalReduction.scalar l E X d n P) ≫
              (ringedKoszulRightUnitIso (ring l E X) (complex l E X P)).inv =
            (ringedKoszulRightUnitIso (ring l E X) (complex l E X P)).inv ≫
              ringedSingletonKoszulPower (ring l E X) t (complex l E X P) n
